verdict.reasoning: Headache duration and location are stated: “Around three days ago maybe” and “it kind of feels all over my head, but like mainly around my right eye,” which corresponds to global with right peri-orbital predominance.
Patient says “it is there all the time, but like sometimes it's stronger” (constant with flares) and rates it “probably an 8” on a 1–10 scale.

Patient describes gradual onset at work and worse next morning: “it developed gradually… it just started when I was at work and by the end of the day it was… a lot… Then I woke up the next morning like it was even, even worse.”
Photophobia is described: “now like light is quite annoying my eyes.” When asked, “does it hurt to look at bright lights?” patient answers, “Yeah, yeah, it hurts.”
Visual phenomena at onset are reported: “just when it started I got this like weird shooting lights.”

Fact states nausea without vomiting. Transcript: Doctor asks “Any nausea or any vomiting?” Patient: “Well, basically I'm sick with the headache, but I. No vomiting.” She does not clearly confirm nausea; saying “I'm sick with the headache” is ambiguous and not explicitly nausea.

Patient denies vision loss: Doctor asks “Have you had any loss of vision or blurry vision?” Patient: “Not loss of vision, I wouldn't say. It's just like some lights from shooting light speed.” No blurring is endorsed.
Doctor: “Any neck pain or neck stiffness?” Patient: “No.”
Doctor: “And any difficulty with speaking or speech?” Patient: “No.”
Doctor: “Any difficulty with weakness in your arms and legs?” Patient: “No.” This supports no focal weakness.
Doctor: “Any recent head injuries at all?” Patient: “No.”
Doctor: “Any temperatures or fevers?” Patient: “No.”
Doctor: “Any rashes at all on your skin?” Patient: “No, none of that I've noticed.”
Impact on concentration is described: “It's hard to focus though, so I had to take a couple of days off work actually.”
Missed work is stated: “It's hard to focus though, so I had to take a couple of days off work actually.”
Patient modified screen use: “I work with computers a lot, so it kind of is difficult to focus. I had to like reduce the brightness of my screen.”
Prior headaches responded to ibuprofen, current one does not: “usually after I take ibuprofen, it kind of goes away… But this time it's just not.”

No other medical history is given. Doctor asks, “Do you have any other medical history?” Patient: “I think so. It's just a headache.” No surgical history is mentioned anywhere, so lack of PMH/PSH is supported as not documented.
Doctor: “do you take any regular medication?” Patient: “No.”

Patient: “So I tried ibuprofen. So I took like a few for the last two days, basically. But it doesn't really help.” Doctor clarifies dose: “How many tablets did you take of ibuprofen?” Patient: “Three a day.” This supports three times a day for two days without effect.
Doctor: “Do you have any allergies to any medications?” Patient: “Not that I know of.”
Seasonal worsening of mother’s migraines: “my mom's is like quite bad. Usually when there's like a season changing and stuff like that, it's… takes her out for a few days.”
Sister’s migraines are infrequent: “my sister's like, better. Like it kind of is very rare.”
Living situation: Doctor: “Who lives at home with you?” Patient: “I live with housemates, so three of them.”
Occupation: “Yeah, so I work well, I work in it, so I work with computers a lot.”
Doctor: “Do you wear glasses?” Patient: “Yes, I do.”
Eye exam history: Doctor: “Have you had a recent eye check done? Eye test?” Patient: “No, I've been wearing them since I was five.”
Mild work stress: Doctor asks about stress; Patient: “Well, it's been a bit stressful kicking off a new project, but yeah, nothing out of the ordinary really.” This reflects mild/moderate stress.
Smoking: Doctor: “do you drink or smoke at all?” Patient: “I socially smoke.”
Alcohol: Patient: “and I drink. Not only socially.” Doctor summarizes “Only socially” but patient’s own statement supports drinking not only socially.

Doctor’s assessment: “I do think this could be a headache very similar to migraine… Given your mum and your sister also have migraines.” Photophobia and visual phenomena (“weird shooting lights”) are described. Duration three days and 8/10 severity are documented earlier.

Refractory to suboptimal NSAID dose: tried ibuprofen three per day for two days with no relief; doctor notes dosing concern: “my only worry is I'm not sure whether you're taking the correct dose. You can take up to two tablets three times a day.”
No red flags: Patient denies fever, neck pain/stiffness, neurologic deficits, and head injury. Doctor specifically checks for these, and they are all answered “No.”
Doctor: “You try the ibuprofen… You can take up to two tablets three times a day. Or I can prescribe you something stronger like naproxen, which is another anti inflammatory.”
Doctor: “We can also add in other painkillers like paracetamol or codeine, which might be helpful as well.”
Codeine prescribed: After discussing, doctor says, “Okay. I think it's only worth looking as I can give you a prescription for that today,” referring to codeine mentioned by patient.
Headache diary advice: “it may be worth keeping a headache diary so we can try and work out… if there's any triggers which could be causing your headaches to become worse.”
Eye test recommendation: “if you feel like your eyes are straining, I would always recommend having a repeat eye test done.”

Follow-up timing: “I'd like you to come back and see me in about a week's time. Week to two weeks time… In the meantime, if your headaches aren't getting any better or they're getting worse, you know, I want you to give me a call or come back and see me sooner.”

Safety net advice: “If you have any problems with your vision or weakness in your arms and legs, or you're just not feeling very well, just give me a call and come back and see me.” This covers new/worsening visual changes, focal weakness, or systemic illness.
Follow-up plan restated: “come back and see me in about a week's time. Week to two weeks time… if your headaches aren't getting any better or they're getting worse… come back and see me sooner.”
